column1: # rel(t?) -- THE RELATION CONSTRAINT, SITED ON THE FIELD
# (docs/design/RELATIONS.0.md §3.2, replacing refer()'s per-element
# spelling). Its value is one address, a LIST of addresses, or a MAP
# whose string leaves are addresses; every leaf goes through the refer
# machinery, so pending resolution, type flow and link stamping are
# one path. The PREDICATE of every edge is the key the rel() sits on --
# declared once, never inferred from the path. Columns:
# name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect
# Every expectation was obtained by running BOTH engines and diffing.
rel-scalar
rel-list
column3: a: id() & {}\nb: id() & {}\ns: id() & {dependsOn: rel() & [a, b]}

column1: rel-map-labelled
# TWO STATEMENTS OF ONE FIELD, in either order: the constraint from
# one, the addresses from the other. The reversed row is what the
# container hand-off arms exist for -- whichever side the fold hands
# the drive, the relation rewrites the container.
rel-two-statements
rel-two-statements-reversed
# THE SCHEMA IDIOM. An unmet rel() is DONE -- its own settled residual,
# like min(1) -- which is what lets a type() body carry one and still
# settle (the property refer() lacks, G4 phase 4). The data side stays
# plain strings.
rel-schema-optional
rel-schema-optional-absent
rel-unmet-canon
# THE FLOW: rel(t) unifies t into each target, so referring to
# something as a kind MAKES it that kind, and a contradiction is an
# ordinary located error at the entity.
rel-flow-admits
rel-flow-refuses
# REFUSALS, each with its own code.
rel-address-not-a-string
rel-address-scalar-direct
rel-unresolved
# Nested containers descend: leaves at any depth are addresses.
rel-nested-map
# An unmet REQUIRED rel refuses at generation, as any unresolved
# residual does; the optional form (rel-schema-optional-absent) drops.
rel-unmet-required
# Two rel() at one field: one relation, both types.
rel-meets-rel
# A KIND met before the value is HELD, and meets the link once there
# is one -- refer's own held rule.
rel-holds-a-kind
# The MAP-drives order (the map twin of rel-two-statements-reversed):
# whichever side the fold hands the drive, the relation rewrites.
rel-map-drives
# A rel in a spread template is cloned per destination.
rel-in-spread-template
# A nil formed beside the rel rides through it.
rel-meets-nil
# A non-string scalar anywhere in the conjunct is refused by the
# relation, whichever term the fold hands it first.
rel-conjunct-non-string
# TWO rel() AT ONE FIELD MERGE INTO ONE RELATION -- both types, both
# held constraints -- whatever order the statements arrive in. The
# order rows pin the fix for unite's equal-scalar shortcuts, which
# matched two settled rels (peg equally absent) and silently dropped
# one side's type and held.
rel-two-at-one-field
rel-two-merged-canon
rel-two-typed-canon
rel-two-held-canon
rel-two-held-order-canon
rel-two-held-both-canon
rel-two-held-resolves
# A rel in LIST-ELEMENT position has no usable field key -- the
# predicate needs a keyed field -- so its links are unlabelled and the
# graph falls back to path inference. It still resolves.
rel-in-list-element
rel-in-list-element-canon
# One rel absorbing two held constraints in one fold carries both.
rel-two-held-fold-canon
rel-two-held-fold-admits
column3: x: id(a) & {}\ns: {d: rel() & re("^a") & re("a$")}\ns: {d: a}

column1: # Held constraints meet the LINK: on a container value they refuse
# loudly (both ports agree) rather than deferring to the rewritten
# list -- the recorded boundary of the held channel.
rel-held-on-container
# The PREDICATE is a D-1 NAME: a list index or a key outside the name
# grammar stamps nothing, and the edge falls back to the graph's path
# inference -- identically in both ports (a list index is a number in
# TS and a string in Go, so the D-1 test is also the parity guard).
rel-at-root-unresolved
rel-at-root-container
# A rel restated after the container already met one is absorbed by
# the merged relation; the restatement changes nothing.
rel-restated-after-container
# A reference-copy of a settled relation field carries its stamped
# links, and a rel() meeting the copy leaves stamped leaves alone --
# the no-op that makes a second application safe.
rel-over-linked-copy
# Held constraints apply PER LEAF: a re() on the relation constrains
# every address, never the container that holds them -- found by the
# service catalog, whose re("^svc_") met the whole list and refused
# it. The refusal is located at the failing element.
rel-held-flows-per-leaf
rel-held-refuses-a-leaf
# A rel(t) whose t names a SIBLING of its own schema bag resolves
# (BUGS.md §53, fixed): the reference walk sees through the pending
# hide()/type() wrapper, so the bag no longer deadlocks on itself.
rel-sibling-shape
